How far apart are the two drivings!

﴿Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾. It was said: the wāw here is the wāw of conjunction (ʿatf), coordinating with a previous clause, and the response (jawab) is omitted. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, they were made happy, and its gates were opened. Omitting the response is eloquent in the speech of the Arabs. He recited the verse of Imru' al-Qays [[The verse is by Imru' al-Qays. "Tamūtu jamī'uhu" means that a sick person's soul does not leave all at once, but dies gradually, piece by piece, and this is the meaning of "tusāqitu anfusā".]]:

"Had it been a soul that dies all at once...
But it is a soul that falls away, soul by soul."

Here the response of "law" is omitted, and the implied meaning is "it would have been easier." Al-Zajjaj said: "Until, when they reach it" means they entered it, and this is close to the first view. It was also said: the wāw is superfluous. The Kufans said this, but it is an error according to the Basrans. It has been said that the presence of the wāw is evidence that the gates were opened for them before they arrived, because of their honour with Allah the Exalted, and the sense is: until, when they reach it while its gates are already open, as evidenced by His words: ﴿Gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them﴾ [Sad: 50]. The wāw is omitted in the account of the people of the Fire, because they were made to stand over the Fire, and its gates were opened after their standing, as a humiliation and a terrifying of them. This was mentioned by al-Mahdawi, and al-Nahhas related its meaning before him. Al-Nahhas said: As for the wisdom in affirming the wāw in the second and omitting it from the first, some scholars have spoken on it with a statement that I know no one has preceded him in, namely that when Allah the Mighty and Majestic said about the people of the Fire: "Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened," this indicates that it was closed; and when He said about the people of the Garden: "Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened," this indicates that it was open before they came to it. And Allah knows best. It was also said that this is the wāw of the eight (wāw al-thamāniyah). This is a custom of the Quraysh, that they count from one, saying: five, six, seven and eight; and when they reach seven they say "and eight." This was said by Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He subjected them to it for seven nights and eight days﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7]. And He said: ﴿The penitent, the worshippers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112], then He said of the eighth: ﴿those who enjoin right and forbid wrong﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112]. And He said: ﴿They will say, "They were seven, and their eighth was their dog"﴾ [al-Kahf: 22]. And He said: ﴿Thayyibat and abkar﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]. The discussion of this has already been given in full in "Bara'ah" [[See vol. 8, p. 271, first or second edition.]] and also in "al-Kahf" [[See vol. 10, p. 382 onward, first or second edition.]].

I say: Those who hold that the gates of Paradise are eight have used this verse as evidence, and they cited the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs ablution and completes (or perfects) the ablution [[Yublighu al-wuḍūʾ: he makes the ablution reach its places. Al-wuḍūʾ is with an open wāw. Yusbigh al-wuḍūʾ: he completes it in the prescribed manner; al-wuḍūʾ is with a dammed wāw. (Margin of Muslim.)]], then says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' but the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters by whichever he wishes." Muslim and others related it. al-Tirmidhi also related this hadith of ʿUmar, and in it he said: "Eight gates of Paradise are opened for him on the Day of Resurrection," with an addition, which indicates that the gates of Paradise are more than eight. We have mentioned this in the book al-Tadhkirah, and their number reaches thirteen gates. We also mentioned there the greatness and vastness of its gates, according to what has been transmitted in the hadith on this matter, so whoever wishes may consult it there.

﴿Its keepers will say to them﴾. It was said: the wāw is redundant, and the sense is "until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them: ﴿Peace be upon you; you have been good﴾". That is, in the world. Mujahid said: by obedience to Allah. It was also said: by righteous deeds. Al-Naqqash related it, and the meaning is one. Muqatil said: When they cross the bridge of Hell, they will be detained at a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution will be exacted from some of them against others for wrongs that were between them in the world. When they have been purified and made pure, Ridwan and his companions will say to them: "Peace be upon you," in the sense of a greeting, "You have been good, so enter it, abiding therein." I say: al-Bukhari related this hadith of the bridge in his Jami' from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The believers will be delivered from the Fire, and they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution will be exacted from some of them against others for the wrongs that were between them in the world. When they have been purified and cleansed, permission will be given them to enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will know his dwelling in Paradise better than he knew his dwelling in the world."

Al-Naqqash related: On the gate of Paradise there is a tree from whose trunk two springs gush forth. The believers drink from one of them, and their insides are purified; this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. Then they wash themselves in the other, and their skins become fragrant. At that moment its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding therein." The meaning of this is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿And they will say: "All praise is for Allah, who has made true His promise to us"﴾, that is, when they enter Paradise they will say this. ﴿And has caused us to inherit the land﴾, that is, the land of Paradise. It was said: they inherited the land which would have been the portion of the people of the Fire had they been believers. This was said by Abu al-ʿAliyah, Abu Salih, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and most of the exegetes. It was also said: it is the land of the world, with a reversal of order. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾. It was said: this is from their own words, meaning: how excellent is this reward! It was also said: it is from the words of Allah the Exalted, meaning: how excellent is the reward of the doers of good, this which I have given them.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you will see the angels﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿surrounding﴾, that is, encircling, ﴿the Throne on every side﴾ on that Day, ﴿glorifying their Lord with praise﴾, delighting in that, not worshipping through it; that is, they pray around the Throne in gratitude to their Lord. The word "ḥāffīn" is derived from the "ḥanāfāt" of a thing, its sides. Al-Akhfash said: its singular is ḥāff. Al-Farra' said: it has no singular, since the term applies to them only when they are gathered. The preposition "min" entered upon "ḥawl" because it is a adverbial noun of place (ẓarf), and the verb reaches an adverbial noun of place both with a preposition and without one. Al-Akhfash said: "min" is superfluous, meaning "surrounding the Throne". It is like your saying: "No one came to me," where "min" is for emphasis. Al-Tha'labi said: The Arabs sometimes introduce the particle bāʾ with tasbīḥ and sometimes omit it, so they say: "sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbika" and "sabbiḥ ḥamda Allāh." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1], and He said: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 74].

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. It was also said: it will be judged between the prophets who are brought together with the martyrs, and between their nations, with truth and justice. ﴿And it will be said: "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾, that is, the believers will say: "All praise is for Allah for what He has rewarded us with of His blessings and His kindness, and for giving us victory over those who wronged us." Qatadah said concerning this verse: Allah began the first creation with praise of Himself, saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾. So it is incumbent to follow Him, beginning every matter with His praise and concluding it with His praise. It was also said: the words "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds" are the words of the angels, and according to this view their praise of Allah the Exalted is for His justice and His judgment. It is related from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the last verse of Surah "al-Zumar" on the pulpit, and the pulpit moved twice.

The tafsir of Surah "al-Zumar" is complete.
